findings.title: Storage failure metric mislabeled as legacy duration in Create
findings.body: In DualWriterMode3.Create, when d.Storage.Create returns an error the code records the failure via d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage). The call was to Storage (not Legacy) and no Legacy call has been made yet on this error path, so the metric is being attributed to the wrong backend and the actual Storage error is not counted in the storage metrics. Should call d.recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage) so operators see real Storage failures and do not get spurious legacy failures.

findings.title: Delete metric uses object name as 'kind' label, causing cardinality explosion
findings.body: After a successful Storage.Delete, the success is recorded with d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage). The third argument is the per-object name (e.g. 'foo', 'bar'), not the resource Kind. Every other method in this file (Create, Get, List, Update, DeleteCollection) passes options.Kind for this argument. Using the object name as the kind label creates a new Prometheus time series per deleted object, exploding label cardinality, breaking aggregation by kind, and risking Prometheus OOM under normal traffic. It should be options.Kind.

findings.title: Storage failure metric mislabeled as legacy duration in Update
findings.body: In DualWriterMode3.Update, when d.Storage.Update returns an error the code records the failure via d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage). The call was to Storage, not Legacy, and the Legacy goroutine has not been spawned yet on this error path. The metric is attributed to the wrong backend, hiding real Storage failures from the storage metrics and injecting fake legacy failures. Should be d.recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage).

findings.title: Legacy DeleteCollection result recorded as storage metric
findings.body: In the DeleteCollection legacy goroutine, after d.Legacy.DeleteCollection returns, the result is recorded via d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy). The call was to the Legacy backend, so it should be recorded via d.recordLegacyDuration. As written, every legacy DeleteCollection outcome is reported against the storage metric, hiding legacy-side failures from operators and inflating the storage success/error counts.

findings.title: Update doc comment implies sequential legacy write
findings.body: The comment on DualWriterMode3.Update reads 'writes first to Storage and then to LegacyStorage', but the actual implementation dispatches the legacy call in a goroutine after the storage call returns, so it is asynchronous and not strictly 'then' in wall-clock order. The comment is misleading for readers trying to understand Mode 3 semantics (and the PR description explicitly calls out that the legacy write is async 'just as a safe measure').
